**(1) First message**

```text
gauntlet: question
The framing holds: I checked lib/notify.ts#post and traced both caller paths. jobs/report.ts inlines the same send, and jobs/digest.ts calls post with a message only. Both paths share one contract: a `[notice] ` prefix, POST to notify.invalid, and two attempts that rethrow on the second failure. The gather draft found no extra loader or runtime dependency, and none of these three files imports one.

Premise note. The supported premises are these:
- lib/notify.ts#post owns formatting and retries but hard-codes `channel: "general"` (lib/notify.ts:2).
- jobs/report.ts duplicates that body construction and retry loop, changing only the channel (jobs/report.ts:2-6).
- jobs/digest.ts relies on the general default by calling `post("Daily digest")` (jobs/digest.ts:2).

No premise was disproved or corrected. The one unverified premise is whether post has callers outside these fixtures. My search covered only the supplied files, so I'll carry that as an assumption that digest is the only other caller. I am also assuming no new notification service, since the shared helper already owns this path. Both points go into the draft.

Which caller-compatibility contract should post offer?
A) an optional channel argument that defaults to general, so existing calls are untouched
B) a required channel argument, with general passed explicitly at every existing call site
C) other - name it
Recommendation: A - digest keeps working unchanged, and report can drop its inline copy.
```

**(2) Approaches message**

No implicit dependency was recorded as missing or not checkable. The traces covered the helper and both callers, and the only open item is the assumption that digest is post's only other caller.

The axis between these approaches is where the general default lives: inside the helper, or at each call site. That choice sets the caller blast radius.

**Recommended: optional channel on the shared helper (reuse-only).** lib/notify.ts#post is the nearly-fitting shared path. Its one gap is the fixed channel. Adding an optional `channel` parameter that defaults to `"general"` closes that gap with no new construct. jobs/report.ts then calls `post(message, channel)` and deletes its inline formatting and retry loop, so retries live in one place again. jobs/digest.ts is untouched and keeps general. The blast radius is one signature change and one caller rewrite.
Removes: jobs/report.ts inline body construction and retry loop (inline copy of post)
Adds: optional `channel` parameter defaulting to `"general"` on lib/notify.ts#post; jobs/report.ts call site `post(message, channel)`; a post test covering the default channel, an explicit channel, and the two-attempt retry
Pattern: follows the owning notification path at lib/notify.ts:1 and removes the duplicated send in jobs/report.ts:2-6

**Alternative: required channel argument (drops the assumption that the helper owns a default).** post takes `channel` as a required parameter. digest passes `"general"` explicitly, and report calls `post(message, channel)`, also removing its inline copy. Every send then states its channel, which reads clearly. The cost is a wider blast radius: every existing caller must change, starting with jobs/digest.ts:2. If other callers exist outside the fixtures, each one breaks until it is updated, and the `"general"` literal spreads across call sites instead of living in one default.
Removes: jobs/report.ts inline body construction and retry loop; the hard-coded `"general"` inside lib/notify.ts#post
Adds: required `channel` parameter on lib/notify.ts#post; explicit `"general"` argument at jobs/digest.ts; jobs/report.ts call site `post(message, channel)`; a post test covering an explicit channel and the two-attempt retry, plus a digest test asserting general
Pattern: follows lib/notify.ts as the owner but pushes the default out to callers, touching every call site (jobs/digest.ts:2)

Keeping report's inline copy is not an approach. It is the duplication this change exists to remove, beside a shared helper that nearly fits (jobs/report.ts:2-6 vs lib/notify.ts:2-6).

I recommend the optional argument because it meets every recorded requirement: report reaches its requested channel, retries stay shared, and default-channel calls stay compatible. It also touches only the caller that needs the change. I would flip to the required argument if you want every send to name its channel explicitly. I would also flip if it turns out post has no callers beyond digest, so the wider blast radius costs almost nothing.

### 1. First message

The framing holds: the supplied primary code and recorded traces cover `lib/notify.ts#post`, the inline report delivery in `jobs/report.ts`, and the default-channel call in `jobs/digest.ts`. They confirm that formatting and the two-attempt retry behavior are duplicated, while the shared helper fixes delivery to `general`. The recorded tracing found no additional loader or runtime dependency.

The requested outcome does not require a new notification service: the existing helper can own channel selection as well as formatting and retries. No load-bearing premise remains contradicted or unverified in the supplied observations.

Your recorded decisions keep this framing: preserve retry behavior and other callers’ default-channel behavior, allow an optional channel argument, and compare it with a required argument that makes existing callers select `general` explicitly. No further clarification is needed.

### 2. Approaches message

I recommend **A: extend the existing helper with an optional channel argument**. The distinction between these approaches is where the default-channel policy lives: inside the shared helper or explicitly at every caller. Neither requires a new service, and both remove the report job’s duplicate delivery implementation.

No implicit dependency was recorded as missing or uncheckable; the supplied traces cover the helper and both caller paths.

**A) Optional channel argument, defaulting to `general` — minimal reuse-only change**

Change the signature to `post(message: string, channel: string = "general")`, and use that channel in the existing payload. Make `report(message, channel)` delegate to `post(message, channel)`. Leave `digest()` unchanged.

This preserves both source compatibility and observable behavior for existing one-argument callers. The helper retains ownership of `[notice]` formatting, the endpoint, two attempts on rejected requests, and propagation of the final error. The trade-off is that an omitted channel remains an implicit choice of `general`.

Removes: the inline payload construction, request, and retry loop from `jobs/report.ts`.
Adds: a defaulted channel parameter and its payload use in `lib/notify.ts#post`; a helper import and delegation call in `jobs/report.ts`.
Pattern: consolidates duplicated behavior into its existing owner, `lib/notify.ts#post`, while preserving the one-argument contract used by `jobs/digest.ts`.

**B) Required channel argument, with explicit `general` at existing callers**

Change the signature to `post(message: string, channel: string)`. Delegate report delivery to that helper and update `digest()` to call `post("Daily digest", "general")`.

This drops the assumption that the shared API must retain an implicit default. It preserves digest delivery to `general` and the existing retry behavior, but changes the source contract for every one-argument caller. In the supplied caller set, digest requires an additional edit. Channel selection becomes visible at each call site, at the cost of broader migration and distributing default-policy choices among callers.

Removes: the inline payload construction, request, and retry loop from `jobs/report.ts`; the helper’s hard-coded channel selection.
Adds: a required channel parameter and its payload use in `lib/notify.ts#post`; a helper import and delegation call in `jobs/report.ts`; an explicit `"general"` argument in `jobs/digest.ts`.
Pattern: keeps delivery mechanics centralized in `lib/notify.ts#post`, but deliberately replaces the implicit-default calling contract demonstrated by `jobs/digest.ts`.

I would choose **B** only if explicit channel selection at every call site becomes a requirement; otherwise **A** delivers the requested behavior with less caller disruption.
